programme: SOX17, HOXB5 and YAP1 form an endothelial-specification/angiogenic transcriptional module: SOX17 sets endothelial/vascular cell identity, HOXB5 induces the classic angiogenic effector genes KDR (VEGFR2), ANGPT2 and TNC downstream of that identity, and YAP1 (the Hippo-pathway effector) converts mechanical and flow-related cues into the same angiogenic transcriptional output. LRRFIP1, acting through PDGFA/EGFR/KRAS, supplies the growth-factor signalling that expands the vessel-associated mural-cell compartment (pericytes/smooth muscle) recruited by this angiogenic programme.
role_in_a: In cardiovascular disease, endothelial specification and PDGF-driven pericyte/smooth-muscle recruitment underlie plaque neovascularization, vascular wall remodeling and ischemic collateral angiogenesis — the tissue's baseline mechanism for building or repairing vessels.
role_in_b: In glioblastoma, this module drives the tumor's characteristic pathological neovascularization: YAP1-dependent angiogenesis, HOXB5-induced KDR/ANGPT2 expression, SOX17-driven endothelial reprogramming, and LRRFIP1/PDGFA-EGFR signalling for pericyte recruitment together sustain the abnormal, leaky tumor vasculature and contribute to anti-angiogenic treatment resistance.
shared_axis: Both diseases are pathologically defined by aberrant new-vessel formation — ischemic/atherosclerotic disease needs collateral angiogenesis and vessel-wall remodeling in the same molecular terms that a solid tumor needs neovascularization to grow — so recurrence of an endothelial-specification and growth-factor module across independent patient subgroups in both diseases plausibly reflects shared reliance on generic angiogenic machinery rather than a disease-specific pathway unique to either.
reasoning: The module is clearly nameable and strongly placed in glioblastoma by seven independent PMIDs across three of the four carrying factors, including one paper explicitly on YAP-dependent angiogenesis in glioblastoma. But every factor shows 'no association recorded' for cardiovascular disease in Open Targets and no paper retrieved connects any of them to CVD, so the cardiovascular side of the story rests on general knowledge that angiogenesis matters in vascular disease, not on anything in the record — hence moderate rather than strong.
support: 35502183 — glioblastoma prognosis study covering both SOX17 and HOXB5; 33858489 — SOX17/HOXB5 (SRSF1/circATP5B/miR-185-5p/HOXB5 loop) in glioma stem cells; 42507234 — investigates YAP-dependent angiogenesis in glioblastoma directly; 42568372, 42650824, 42014897 — additional YAP1/Hippo-pathway signalling in glioblastoma; 35338570, 37407848 — LRRFIP1 as a glioblastoma prognostic and immune-microenvironment biomarker. none found for cardiovascular disease for any of these factors.
how_to_falsify: Knock down SOX17, HOXB5, YAP1 and LRRFIP1 in a cardiovascular-relevant angiogenesis assay (e.g., endothelial sprouting or ischemic hindlimb collateral formation) and check whether KDR/ANGPT2 induction and vessel growth are unaffected there while remaining essential in a parallel glioblastoma vasculature assay — if the module is dispensable in the vascular-disease context, the shared-axis claim fails. A positive control would be ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq comparing occupancy of these factors at KDR and ANGPT2 loci in CVD-patient endothelium versus GBM tumor endothelium.
caveats: The blood|brain tissue pairing biases retrieval toward glioblastoma, which has a much larger dedicated literature; none of the four carrying factors has any documented cardiovascular-disease evidence in this record, so 'supported' leans entirely on textbook angiogenesis biology, not retrieved data. Only 4 independent cohort pairs underlie the 64 patient-group comparisons, so recurrence fractions (e.g., SOX17 38/64) partly reflect within-cohort correlation rather than broad independent replication. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed several classic endothelial master regulators (KLF2, ERG, STAT5B, NR3C1, FOS, ESR1, FOXO1, NFATC1, KLF6, STAT3) that would ordinarily anchor a vascular story, meaning this account had to be built from second-tier factors; and WWTR1 (TAZ, YAP1's close paralog) appeared in only one patient group (single-view), so the Hippo-pathway angiogenesis signal should not be generalized beyond YAP1 itself.
